_meta.description: Geolocations for LSD theatre codes. Coordinates are WGS84 decimal degrees for the historical building's modern location (or closest surviving identifiable point). Compound codes (dlking's, dlordg, dldg, dllif, dlandlif, dlordg, dldglif, dlorlif, bforsf) are intentionally omitted — they resolve to their constituent codes at query time. Sentinels (none, None) are also omitted.

precisionLevels.exact: Known street address or surviving building footprint
precisionLevels.approximate: Known district/street but exact address uncertain
precisionLevels.unknown: Venue not locatable from available sources

dl.source: Theatre Royal, Drury Lane — standing building on Catherine Street / Russell Street. Multiple rebuilds (1674 Wren, 1794 Holland, 1812 Wyatt) on essentially the same footprint.

cg.source: Royal Opera House, Bow Street, Covent Garden — occupies the site of the Theatre Royal Covent Garden from 1732 (Rich's house, rebuilt 1809 and 1858). Vol 1 'CG' references the locale; from 1732 onwards it is the theatre.

hay.source: Theatre Royal Haymarket — standing building, Haymarket street. Vanbrugh's 'little theatre' opened 1720; rebuilt by Nash 1821 a few doors south on the same street.

king's.source: Queen's / King's Theatre, Haymarket — site now occupied by Her Majesty's Theatre at the corner of Haymarket and Pall Mall. Vanbrugh's opera house opened 1705; burned 1789; rebuilt on same site.

lif.source: Lincoln's Inn Fields Theatre (Portugal Street / Portugal Row), converted from Lisle's Tennis Court. Used by Davenant 1661-71, Betterton 1695-1705, Rich 1714-32, Giffard 1732-33. Site now covered by the Royal College of Surgeons / Portugal Street.

gf.source: Goodman's Fields Theatre, Ayliffe Street (later Leman Street area), Whitechapel. Odell's 1729 house and Giffard's 1732 rebuild; site near modern Leman Street / Alie Street junction, where Garrick debuted in 1741.

queen's.source: Queen's Theatre, Haymarket (Vanbrugh, 1705) — renamed King's in 1714. Same site as 'king's'.

dg.source: Dorset Garden Theatre (Duke's Theatre / Queen's Theatre), opened 1671 on the Thames between the Temple and Blackfriars, off Salisbury Court / Dorset Street. Site now covered by the Mermaid Theatre area, Blackfriars Embankment.

bridges.source: First Theatre Royal on Bridges Street (Killigrew, 1663), destroyed by fire 1672. Site on Bridges (now Catherine) Street, immediately adjacent to the later DL building.

vere.source: Theatre in Vere Street (Gibbon's Tennis Court), used by Killigrew's King's Company 1660-63. Site off Clare Market / Vere Street, near modern Aldwych / Kingsway (Clare Market was cleared c. 1900 for the LSE / Aldwych redevelopment).

sw.source: Sadler's Wells Theatre, Rosebery Avenue, Islington — continuous site since Richard Sadler's 1683 music house; current building is the 1998 reconstruction on the same plot.

nwc.source: New Wells, London Spa, Clerkenwell — near Exmouth Street / Rosoman Street, close to Sadler's Wells. Exact plot not firmly identified.

nwgf.source: New Wells, Goodman's Fields — on Lemon Street / Ayliffe Street area, Whitechapel. Rival to the licensed GF house in the 1740s.

nwls.source: New Wells, Lemon Street (present-day Leman Street area), Whitechapel.

nwmf.source: New Wells, Mayfair — near the traditional May Fair site at Shepherd Market.

nwsm.source: New Wells, Shepherd's Market, Mayfair — in the old May Fair ground cleared in the 1730s-40s.

smmf.source: Shepherd's Market, Mayfair — same locale as the May Fair grounds.

bf.source: Bartholomew Fair — held annually in West Smithfield, City of London, from 1133 until 1855. Booths pitched across the open market square.

sf.source: Southwark Fair — held in the Borough, on and around Borough High Street between St Margaret's Hill and St George's Church, abolished 1762.

mf.source: May Fair — held at Shepherd Market (Brook Field), off Piccadilly, suppressed as a nuisance from 1708 but revived intermittently to 1764.

mef.source: Mile End Fair — held on Mile End Green, east of the City, near modern Mile End tube.

meg.source: Mile End Green — open space alongside Mile End Road, used for drolls and sideshows.

tc.source: Tottenham Court Fair — held at the junction of Tottenham Court Road and the New Road (now Euston Road), near the village of Tottenham Court.

wf.source: Vol 1 'WF' = Music School, White Fryars (Whitefriars, between Fleet Street and the Thames, west of Dorset Garden). Vol 3 'WF' = Welch Fair, held in London (site uncertain). Coordinate given is for the Whitefriars precinct, the Vol 1 reading.

marly.source: Marylebone Gardens — bounded by Marylebone High Street, Weymouth Street, Beaumont Street and Devonshire Street; closed 1778, site now Devonshire Place / Beaumont Street.

ranelagh.source: Ranelagh Gardens, Chelsea — site now within the grounds of the Royal Hospital Chelsea (Ranelagh Gardens). The Rotunda stood where the modern gardens lie, east of the hospital.

vaux.source: Vauxhall (Spring) Gardens, Lambeth — bounded by modern Kennington Lane and Goding Street; most of the site is now Spring Gardens / Vauxhall Pleasure Gardens park.

pan.source: Pantheon, Oxford Street — James Wyatt's 1772 assembly rotunda at 173 Oxford Street; site now occupied by the Marks & Spencer Pantheon store.

pant.source: The Pantheon, Oxford Street — same site as 'pan'.

roy.source: Royalty Theatre, Well Street (now Ensign Street), Wellclose Square, Goodman's Fields — opened by John Palmer 1787.

chr.source: China Hall Theatre, Lower Road, Rotherhithe — short-lived 1776-78 converted warehouse; Lower Road is now Jamaica Road / Lower Road, Rotherhithe.

nursery.source: The Nursery — training playhouses at Moorfields, Bunhill, or Hatton Garden (the key is ambiguous). Coordinate given is for Bunhill / Moorfields, the best-attested Restoration nursery site.

redbull.source: Red Bull Theatre, St John Street / Red Bull Yard, Clerkenwell — Elizabethan playhouse reused briefly 1660-64. Site approximately at modern Hayward's Place, off St John Street.

salisbury.source: Salisbury Court Theatre, Whitefriars — converted barn/playhouse in Salisbury Court, off Fleet Street; used 1660-61 before the company moved to LIF. Now the Salisbury Court / Dorset Rise area.

cockpit.source: Cockpit in Drury Lane (Phoenix), Pit Place / Pitt's Head Mews off Drury Lane. Used briefly 1660-62 by Rhodes / Davenant companies.

atcourt.source: Whitehall or St James's Palace (Court performance). Coordinate given for the Palace of Whitehall / Banqueting House on Whitehall; many court performances took place in the Hall Theatre, Whitehall (destroyed 1698), but St James's Palace was also used.

stjames.source: St James's Palace, Pall Mall — standing building.

hc.source: Hampton Court Palace — standing royal residence.

kg.source: Kew Gardens / Kew Palace, Richmond upon Thames.

oxford.source: Oxford University — Sheldonian and college halls used by touring companies. Coordinate for the Sheldonian / central university area.

dover.source: Dover, England — 1670 Duke's Company performance for Charles II at the Treaty of Dover.

ri.source: Richmond — various Richmond-upon-Thames venues used by summer touring companies. Coordinate for Richmond Green, the usual playhouse site (Cibber's / Chapman's Richmond Theatre stood on Richmond Hill / the Green).

richmond.source: New Wells Richmond — Richmond-upon-Thames, site on or near Richmond Green / The Rosary.

riw.source: Richmond Wells — on Richmond Hill, spa and music room, 1696-c.1755.

acad.source: Cibber's Histrionic Academy on the Bowling Green, Richmond Hill — Richmond-upon-Thames.

ks.source: Kingston, The Playhouse by the Hand — Kingston upon Thames; exact plot unknown.

hamm.source: Windsor Castle Inn, King Street, Hammersmith — King Street is the modern A315, Hammersmith Broadway area.

rlsn.source: Red-Lion Inn, Lordship Road (now Lordship Park / Stoke Newington Church Street area), Stoke Newington.

cii.source: Crown Inn, Lower Street (now Essex Road), Islington.

och.source: Old Crown Inn, Highgate — location not precisely documented.

whf.source: White Horse Inn, Parsons Green, Fulham — at the south end of Parsons Green.

khs.source: King's Head Inn, Borough High Street, Southwark — galleried coaching inn at 25-27 Borough High Street (site adjacent to the George Inn).

wlws.source: White-Lion Inn, Wych Street — Wych Street was the former south continuation of Drury Lane, cleared c. 1900 for the Aldwych redevelopment.

ham.source: The Long Room, Hampstead — on Well Walk, Hampstead (the assembly room attached to Hampstead Wells).

haw.source: Hampstead Wells — Well Walk, Hampstead; spa and assembly rooms from 1698.

che.source: Chelsea — general locale; specific venues not differentiated.

chelsea.source: Priest's Boarding School in Chelsea — exact address unrecorded.

houn.source: Hounslow — coaching town west of London.

mo.source: Moorfields — open ground immediately north of the City wall (now Finsbury Circus / Moorgate).

sou.source: Southwark — general locale; Borough High Street and environs.

ntw.source: New Theatre, Mr Bradley's Distiller, Old Gravel Lane (now Wapping Lane), Wapping.

bg.source: Bedford Gate, Charles Street, Covent Garden — Charles Street is now Wellington Street.

vendu.source: Vendu (auction room), Charles Street, Covent Garden — same street as BG.

pcr.source: Great Piazza Coffee Room, Covent Garden — at the north-east corner of Covent Garden Piazza.

pcgr.source: Great Room, Peter's Court — off St Martin's Lane, near Long Acre.

dc.source: Dorset Court, off Salisbury Court / Dorset Rise, Whitefriars.

eb.source: Essex Buildings — east side of Essex Street off the Strand, on the former Essex House site.

mt.source: Middle Temple — Middle Temple Hall, off Fleet Street.

li.source: Lincoln's Inn — the Inn of Court, Chancery Lane.

mr.source: Mercers' Hall, Ironmonger Lane, City of London — standing building.

lei.source: Leicester House — formerly on the north side of Leicester Square/Fields; demolished 1792.

bellsize.source: Belsize House, Hampstead — Restoration mansion used as a pleasure resort from 1720; coordinate for Belsize Park.

haygr.source: Great Room, Haymarket — on Haymarket street, near the Theatre Royal.

cgr.source: Coignand's Great Room — at Coignand's dancing school, Leicester Square / Panton Street area (exact address varies by year).

cds.source: Coignand's Dancing School — same locale as 'cgr'.

globe.source: Globe Tavern, Fleet Street — on the south side of Fleet Street near the Temple; historic coffee/tavern site.

cr.source: Crown and Anchor Tavern, The Strand — on the corner of Arundel Street; major 18th-century concert and political-club venue, burned 1854.

crt.source: Crown Tavern behind the Royal Exchange — in Threadneedle Street / Cornhill area, City of London.

ct.source: Castle Tavern, Paternoster Row (or the Paternoster Row / Holborn tavern of the same name) — coordinate given for Paternoster Row, the most-attested Castle Tavern for music meetings.

dt.source: Devil Tavern, Fleet Street — at No. 2 Fleet Street, by Temple Bar; Ben Jonson's 'Apollo Room' tavern; demolished 1787.

gv.source: George and Vulture Tavern, Castle Court / Lombard Street, City of London — standing building.

sun.source: Sun Tavern — 17th/18th-c. tavern behind the Royal Exchange, Cornhill (several venues of the name).

gt.source: Vol 2 'Greyhound Tavern' vs Vol 3 'George Tavern' — different venues sharing the code. Coordinate given for the Greyhound, off Fleet Street / Holborn area (Vol 2 reading).

ttt.source: Three Tuns Tavern / Three Tuns and Bull Head — several of this name; the musical-meetings Three Tuns was on Chandos Street / Holborn area.

bht.source: Bull Head Tavern — Cheapside, City of London.
